variants.asks: the retarded force and the metric both correct gravity for motion. Are those two effects, one effect twice, or one of them short of something?

probes.asks: what are this lattice's own numbers - how many ways out of a point, how many charges a pulse lets go, how long a turn takes?
probes.found: fcc-12: D = 3, DEG = 12, SHEET = 6, CYCLE = 6 - counts, not measurements

measured.name: D
measured.note: how many dimensions fcc-12 has

measured.name: DEG
measured.note: the ways out of a point on fcc-12 - the exits it has, counted

measured.name: SHEET
measured.note: the exits with no component along the pulsing axis, which is what a source emits over. NOT DEG, which is 12

measured.name: CYCLE
measured.note: how many steps go round the ring of a turn on fcc-12

measured.name: slice
measured.note: a turn sweeps a PLANE, and a plane needs two dimensions - so what a turn lives in is min(D, 2), which is 2 here and stops growing at 2 however many dimensions are added

measured.name: \bar{c}
measured.note: a step's worth of lean is what one annihilation buys a path, and a step is \bar{c} - one cell a tick, the lattice's own speed. Its value in those units is one, which is a statement about the units and not about the quantity

probes.asks: put the counted metric and general relativity through one integrator. How far does a perihelion move, how far is light bent, and do the two metrics agree?
probes.found: the counted metric gives 6.07 sixths of general relativity's perihelion advance (worst orbit off by 0.11), and bends light by 1.0006 of what general relativity does - through the same integrator, with Newton closing to 5.1e-4

measured.name: sixths
measured.note: the counted metric's perihelion advance against general relativity's, over 3 orbits: r0 60 gives 6.08, r0 120 gives 6.11, r0 240 gives 6.01. Six sixths is general relativity's own answer

measured.name: Newton's advance, same integrator
measured.note: integrated as the actual inverse-square law - a Kepler ellipse closes, so this is the integrator's own noise and the scale against which the other two mean anything

measured.name: bending
measured.note: light bent past the mass, counted metric against general relativity, at impact parameters 200 (1.0010), 400 (1.0005), 800 (1.0003). General relativity's own answer is 4M/b, which it gives here to 1.013, 1.002, 0.984 of itself

measured.name: retarded/A
measured.note: the metric's time part against the retarded branches, per beta squared, at b=0.01 (1.000089), b=0.05 (1.000089), b=0.1 (1.000089), b=0.2 (1.000089). The spread across speeds is 7.59e-13 - the offset from one is the static term at this radius, not a velocity effect

measured.name: B/A
measured.note: and the metric's SPACE part against the same, which the retarded route has no counterpart for at all

steps.because: so what the retarded route does not account for is the difference, and it is B's term less the clock convention. THE GAP IS NOT A DISAGREEMENT BUT A MISSING TERM: the retarded force is the metric with the space part left out. That is why the two are compared rather than multiplied - multiplying would count A twice and still never mention B
so the metric's whole velocity correction is the two together, 2 beta^{2} - which is what differentiating it gives directly, so the split accounts for all of it
k_{metric} is not a primitive of this theory - it is k_{A} + k_{B}, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

and the piece from the space part B carries another 1.00 beta^{2}. This is space being stretched where the count is high, which is not a statement about when anything arrives - so nothing about travel time can produce it
k_{B} is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

the retarded force carries A's beta^{2} - its two branches and its clock are exactly what a late arrival and a slow clock do - plus a half from whose clock the answer is quoted per, which this folder makes a switch of. That is 3/2 on the receiver's clock and 1 on the lattice's
k_{retard} is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1/2 + k_{A}, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out
1/2 has nothing left in it that varies, so it is 1/2 exactly

missing.says: what the retarded route does not account for, per beta squared

retarded/A.says: the retarded factor against the metric's time part - one means they are the same quantity

k_{metric}.says: the metric's whole velocity correction, per beta squared

k_{A}.says: the part of it from the time part - a slow clock and a late arrival

k_{B}.says: the part from the space part - the stretch, which is not about time at all

F_{g}^{rel}.says: the force with travel time in it

A·B.says: the metric, whose product is one
